issues.description: panLinear/zoomLinear silently coerce invalid domain values to 0, changing numerical output vs prior NaN-propagating behavior
issues.detail: The original code passed `toNumber` directly as the lift function. `toNumber` returns `null` for non-coercible inputs, which propagates as NaN through arithmetic (a meaningful 'invalid' signal). The new `coerceNumber: TransformFn = x => toNumber(x) ?? 0` silently maps null to 0, so `panLinear([null, null], 0.5)` now returns `[0, 0]` instead of `[NaN, NaN]`. This is a real behavioral regression hidden inside a 'just adding types' PR, and the comment in the source explicitly acknowledges it ('Unlike toNumber, coerceNumber always returns a number (never null)'). Callers that branched on NaN to detect bad domains will silently get plausible-looking zeros.

issues.description: Empty-domain error is a breaking API change not flagged in the PR title/changelog
issues.detail: Previously `panLinear([], ...)` returned `[NaN, NaN]` (peek of [] is undefined, arithmetic yields NaN). Now it throws. The PR title says 'refactor' and 'Make transform functions typesafe', but the body buries 'Adds a runtime error when users try to operate on a domain that doesn't have at least 1 value'. Any downstream caller (including other vega packages) that tolerated empty domains will now hard-fail. This either needs a semver-major callout or the change should be reverted to preserve the no-op/NaN behavior.

issues.description: `error()` likely not typed as `never`, so isNonEmpty narrowing may not survive past the guard
issues.detail: The pattern `if (!isNonEmpty(domain)) error('Domain array must not be empty');` only narrows `domain` to `NonEmptyArray<number>` on subsequent lines if `error` has return type `never`. If `error` is typed as `void` or returns anything other than `never`, TypeScript will still see `domain` as `number[]`, and the call `peek(domain)` will pick the `T | undefined` overload, defeating part of the typesafety goal. The PR should either confirm `error`'s signature is `(msg: string) => never` or use `throw` directly.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new error path is partial — only Linear variants covered
issues.detail: New tests cover only `panLinear([])` and `zoomLinear([], null, 2.0)`. The log/pow/symlog variants also call the now-throwing `pan`/`zoom`, but they additionally evaluate `Math.sign(domain[0])` in the wrapper before the guard runs, so their behavior with empty input is worth pinning down with a test (it computes `Math.sign(undefined) = NaN` then throws — fine, but undocumented). Add at least one test per family to lock in the contract.

issues.description: Local `identity` shadows the shared `accessors.identity` for no clear benefit
issues.detail: The original imported `identity` from `./accessors.js`. The new code defines a local `identity: TransformFn = x => x`. Functionally equivalent for numbers, but it diverges from the codebase's single source of truth for the identity accessor and is purely to satisfy `TransformFn`. A cleaner approach is to import the shared identity and cast/assert it as `TransformFn` once, or relax `TransformFn` to `(x: any) => number`.

issues.description: `Domain` return type `[number, number]` is stricter than what callers may currently expect
issues.detail: Original code returned a plain array. The new tuple type `[number, number]` is more precise, but if any consumer typed its variable as `number[]`, assigning is fine; if any consumer destructured a 3rd element (unlikely but possible in JS), TS would now reject it. Worth noting in release notes when this propagates to typed consumers.

issues.description: `peek` overload ordering and `readonly` may not match call site `number[]`
issues.detail: `peek` is overloaded as `readonly [T, ...T[]] -> T` and `readonly T[] -> T | undefined`. Call site passes `domain: number[]` (mutable). Assignability of mutable to readonly should be fine. Once narrowed via `isNonEmpty` to `[number, ...number[]]`, the first overload should match. This is OK but subtle; a quick `tsc --noEmit` check on a consumer should confirm.

dissents.topic: Whether coerceNumber's null-to-0 fallback is a bug or a reasonable simplification

positions.position: It is a behavioral regression: NaN propagation was a meaningful invalid-input signal, and silently coercing to 0 produces plausible-but-wrong outputs. Block merge until reverted or explicitly documented.
Linear pan/zoom on non-numeric domain entries is nonsense input; clamping to 0 is no worse than NaN and avoids downstream NaN poisoning. Acceptable if release-noted.

dissents.topic: Whether throwing on empty domain is the right contract

positions.position: Empty domain has no defined transformation; failing loudly is the correct contract, and prior NaN returns were a latent bug.
This is a public utility package; switching from silent NaN to a thrown error is a breaking change and must be released as such, or guarded behind a flag.
Redefining identity locally violates DRY and duplicates a primitive that has a canonical home in accessors.js.
A locally-typed identity matching TransformFn is clearer than importing-and-casting; the duplication is one line and improves type inference at the call site.

review.summary: The PR claims to be a pure type-safety refactor but introduces two semantic changes: (1) `coerceNumber` replaces `toNumber` as the linear lift function, silently mapping null to 0 instead of propagating NaN, which is a real numerical behavior change; (2) empty domains now throw instead of returning [NaN, NaN], which is a breaking API change for vega-util consumers. The error-guard pattern also depends on `error()` being typed as `never` for TS narrowing to work — worth verifying. Test coverage of the new throw path is limited to Linear variants. Type additions themselves (peek overloads, Domain tuple, TransformFn) look correct, but the PR should either revert the runtime changes to match its 'refactor' framing or be relabeled and release-noted as a behavior change.
